productionChanges.summary: forgePreview(s,id) returns six exact single-item attribute panels, capped reinforcement gains, current affordability/eligibility and costExceedsGoldCap. No engine action changed; it does not draw dice or change persisted state.

Spring choices and newly resolved outcomes now describe a shield floor (Math.max), preserving higher existing shields. Old pending event objects are not rewritten and resolved historical outcome text remains intact.

productionChanges.kind: confirmed boundary UI problem, root owns UI fix
productionChanges.summary: forgeCost may return GOLD_CAP+1 as an unaffordable sentinel; the preview exposes costExceedsGoldCap so the UI cannot falsely promise that one additional coin can fund an impossible purchase. Original price and canAct behavior remain unchanged.

api.interpretation: Single-item displayed stats, not player total stats or guaranteed combat damage. Current ordinary and deep conditional/luck/critical traits do not scale with reinforcement. A low-level relic can gain reinforcement while all item panels remain identical after integer rounding.

naturalMethod: Every journey starts with newGame and normal floor-one equipment. All talent investment, respec, equip, forge and protected fusion use legal engine actions. Full available talent priorities are invested before progress; vitality is capped by test preference at 5 for balanced/resonance/luck or 20 for bulwark. Protected consumption retains the best current-value representative of each catalog ID and excludes equipped, locked and current-loot materials. Different spending changes real RNG consumption and later routes/drops; whole journeys are not isolated causal A/B tests.

sameOpeningForgeCounterfactual.method: Each branch legally forges exactly one different equipped slot from an identical natural forge state. Same forge face, subsequent enemy and combat-opening RNG are asserted. Normal roll-only fight follows.
sameOpeningForgeCounterfactual.finding: All 30 branches still needed the same 1–2 rolls within each opening and took zero direct HP loss. Armor increased capacity/defense but did not improve a demonstrated survival outcome in these samples. Relic reinforcement raised only base attack, not luck/conditional rates.

sameOpeningMaterialExample.note: The high-material example is a read-only exact quote from the same natural fusion state, not a natural random reward guarantee. Consuming seven redundant high-rarity items permanently loses those copies; the strongest of each catalog ID is retained.

limits: Automated policies and fixed seeds do not estimate human win rates, willingness to spend or optimal balance.
No synthetic grants, forced dice, floor skips or enemy tuning were used in natural journeys. Boundary differential scenes are explicitly synthetic.

The 200-floor report was generated before the additive costExceedsGoldCap preview metadata field. Only src/equipment.js source hash differs from final among its listed gameplay files, and the final 1920-case forge differential confirms unchanged gameplay.

The raw 200-floor report counted uniform abilityRoll log strings only. Its phaseWard/firstCritLuck/eliteLuck/gildedSix zeros are NOT_TESTED by that counter and must not be interpreted as no activation. The script has been fixed; both 400-floor reports include correct pre-state/committed-result checks for these four abilities.
Net event spending undercounts full payments immediately followed by a partial refund; the reports document this limitation.
All gameplay benchmark durations were collected during concurrent work and are not performance comparisons.

At 400 floors, investing across five slots and normal safe-material fusion still left 1.46m/1.49m gold. This keeps long-term economy and human-choice value open; it does not justify a blind fee/drop change.
The final UI presentation, browser outcomes and full-suite counts belong to root; they are not implied by these API and engine checks.

research.title: Memory Recognition and Recall in User Interfaces
research.application: Put the current decision’s item attributes, cost and consequences together instead of making players recall an upgrade formula.
